**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Open the parent handle before killing and reaping the child**

On Linux, this test deterministically fails because `command.Wait()` has already reaped the child before `openParent` calls `processIdentity`, so `/proc/<pid>/stat` no longer exists. Reproducing the update package tests produced `process_unix_test.go:52: open /proc/.../stat: no such file or directory`. macOS likewise rejects the nonexistent process. This blocks the Linux/macOS test jobs in `.github/workflows/check.yml`; acquire the parent identity handle while the child is alive, then kill/reap it and verify that `waitParent` observes its exit.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L37-L39](https://github.com/steampixel007/Dipper/blob/fc89d426eb0181481c96adaeafbe04790e59c0c3/AGENTS.md#L37-L39)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve Unix helper failure reports after the application exits**

For Linux/macOS updates that fail after commit, this writes the only failure report to a discarded stream: `preparePlatformUpdate` starts the helper without assigning `command.Stderr`, so Go connects its stderr to the null device. By then the original application has exited, and `Installer.Commit` also ignores the helper's eventual exit status. Consequently, authorization failures, failed restarts, and retained-backup recovery instructions never reach the user or application logs. Persist the failure for the next launch or display it through a desktop notification/dialog instead of relying solely on stderr.
